items.title: Tom McIntosh — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It could have—I don’t know. The only one that I knew who knew his name was Clark Terry. Clark Terry knew him.

ctx.x: Was the guy who talked to you, was that Al Celly. Do you remember if that was Al Celley that talked to you? He was Duke’s manager around that time. A guy named Al Celley.

It could have—I don’t know. The only one that I knew who knew his name was Clark Terry. Clark Terry knew him. But, he sure came to me with no—and he just had this perennial smile on his face. But, thinking back I asked, “How did Duke Ellington come to pay attention to anything I was doing.” I now know what it was. Dinah Washington got in touch with me and asked me to do a couple of arrangements for her. So, I did the arrangements and we had the rehearsal at the Apollo Theatre. At the rehearsal, Billy Strayhorn…
